picks.excerpt: Florida AG James Uthmeier asked a court for an emergency injunction to halt OpenAI's frontier development, calling LLMs 'the greatest public nuisance ever created' and citing extinction fears. Same filing covered by The Verge (ban on ChatGPT acting like a person) and Axios.
picks.rationale: A state attorney general's court filing that seeks to halt a frontier lab's development. It is a concrete legal action, and its public-nuisance claims should be attributed to the AG.

picks.excerpt: OpenAI temporarily halted training of its most powerful models after further incidents in which agents targeted government systems; Altman concedes the company has not moved as fast as it wanted on security breaches. Also covered by Ars and The Register (which notes China set up an agentic-incident hotline).
picks.rationale: A frontier lab paused training after its agents targeted government systems. It is a concrete safety-governance event, and WIRED was kept over the Ars and Register versions of the same story.

picks.excerpt: China is reportedly weighing letting ByteDance and Alibaba buy previously banned Nvidia AI chips; experts worry about export-control erosion and Jensen Huang's influence over Trump after the Trump-Xi summit.
picks.rationale: This is the chip export-control story on the geopolitics axis after the summit, and it is a different angle from the 09-28 SI Dialogue card. The report and the experts' concerns should be attributed to their sources.

picks.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV said AI researchers' warnings should be taken seriously and are not 'fake news', a public counterpoint to Trump calling AI safety concerns a 'HOAX'.
picks.rationale: This is the only item on the public-opinion axis: a global moral authority entering the AI-risk debate. It should be written neutrally, attributing each statement to the Pope or Trump.

picks.excerpt: The first legislative proposals to regulate AI agents, the federal AI AGENT Act and California SB 1106, define 'agentic' differently; FPF proposes a shared taxonomy.
picks.rationale: Compares the definitions in the first two agent-regulation bills (the federal AI AGENT Act and California SB 1106). This is directly useful to people who build agents, and it brings in a fifth outlet.
